reason: Wind blowing over the sea should generate waves that can work on the shore.
expectation: The wind will create waves capable of moving and wearing rock.

effect: Wind-driven waves are now available to act on the coast.
reason: Waves striking the fractured headland should break or loosen basalt for the shore.
expectation: Wave action will produce loose fragments of basalt.

effect: The breaking waves can now act on existing cracks in the rock.
reaction: The result clarifies how waves reach the fractured shore.
reason: The breaking waves should exploit the cracks in the volcanic crust and loosen rock.
expectation: Wave impacts will loosen fragments from the cracked rock.

effect: Wave impacts have freed angular stones that can supply the two shore types.
reaction: The distinction between physical breaking and dissolution is useful.
reason: Further wave action should wear the loose stones into smaller, rounder material.

choice.combine: Angular stones freed from the coast

expectation: The waves will abrade or break the stones into smaller shore material.

effect: Abrasion has produced rounded pebbles that may form the coarse headland shore.
reaction: The reminder that rounding takes repeated collisions is useful.
reason: The rounded pebbles are a plausible fit for the coarse shore at the headland.
expectation: The pebbles will gather into a coarse shore at the headland.

effect: The pebbles formed the coarse headland shore, completing that goal; the sheltered beach remains.
reaction: The explanation of heavier stones being sorted by flow was useful.
reason: I’m unsure which remaining operation will produce beach-sized material, so I’ll check the loose stones.

choice.inspect: Angular stones freed from the coast

expectation: The inspection should show whether the stones can be worn down or transported toward the bay.

effect: The inspection automatically produced dark volcanic sand, which can supply the remaining beach goal.
reaction: It was helpful to see that continued wave abrasion produces sand.
reason: The sheltered bend is the natural place for the dark sand to accumulate into a beach.

choice.with: A sheltered bend in the coast

expectation: The sand will settle in the sheltered bay and form a dark beach.

effect: The sand needed wave-driven transport before it could reach the sheltered bay; the failed attempt automatically produced moving sand.
reaction: I had overlooked the transport step.
reason: The moving sand can plausibly settle where the sheltered bend reduces water movement.

choice.with: A sheltered bend in the coast

expectation: Sand will accumulate in the sheltered bend to form a dark beach.

effect: The transported sand accumulated in the sheltered bend, completing the dark beach and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the two different shores form through sorting and transport.

mostWorthwhile.text: Forming the coarse pebble shore was worthwhile because it showed how flow sorts heavier stones, not just how waves break rock.

leastWorthwhile.text: The direct attempt to make the beach was least worthwhile: I overlooked the transport step, though the feedback automatically advanced it.

surprise.text: I had not expected the sand to require a separate wave-driven transport step before reaching the bay.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt entirely arbitrary; the initially unclear sand-to-beach step gained a physical explanation through wave transport.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to follow more processes where familiar landscapes emerge from interacting physical mechanisms.
